craft_notes: Sthāyin: thirsting to drink and give. Device: comma line 1 kept? Changed: end-dash→comma line 2? Original L3 line2: 'to quaff, what stranger meet? To ladle — world-Lord, who then?' L4: 'to quaff, what stranger meet? To ladle, world-Lord, who then?' (dash→comma). Rejected: 'sip/serve' plain pair — kept quaff/ladle (kept register). Read aloud: lands on close.

lines: Though hymning but the honey-spate whose grace fruits in thee,
to quaff, what stranger meet? To ladle, world-Lord, who then?
l4.sanskrit_cite: kīrtane 'py amṛtaughasya yatprasatteḥ phalaṃ tava tat pātum api ko 'nyo 'laṃ kim u dātuṃ jagatpate

reads_against.argmap: Even in praising, of the nectar-flood — of which favour is your fruit.; That to drink, who else is capable — how much more to give, O world-lord? → None can drink your nectar-fruit, much less give it, but you.
c1_essence: None fit to sip nectar-fruit, much less serve it, but you.
reads_against.l2: Though we hymn but the spate of sweet — whose grace fruits in you — to sip it, what stranger is fit? To serve it round — O world-king, who then?
l3: Though hymning but the honey-spate whose grace fruits in thee —
to quaff, what stranger meet? To ladle — world-Lord, who then?
reads_against.t1: Even in praising, of the nectar-flood — of which favour is your fruit — that to drink, who else is capable — how much more to give, O world-lord?
